sections.html: In its habitat C. molitorella inhabits midwater to bottom depths of running waters. It is found both in fast-flowing sections and in calmer water, during the rainy season even within flooded areas.
As an omnivore it is problem-free in terms of nutrition, although large quantities of food are needed.

If you are interested in a larger growing fish, the mud carp Cirrhinus molitorella, originating from Southeast Asia, could be the right thing for you. In the list of fishing world records it is quoted with a length of 1 m and in Thailand it is known under the name Pa Keng as a strong fighter on the fishing rod. In the aquarium it will not reach this size and can be kept together, for example, with large representatives of the genera Labeo, Osphronemus or Channa. This is aimed at owners of very large aquaria, who can try to house the Southeast Asian riverine fauna in biotope aquaria. With bamboo canes, roots and large stones, beautiful underwater landscapes can be arranged.
